title: Sephiria Weapons & Upgrades (1.0) — Six Branches, Tier Notes, Routes
description: Sephiria weapons guide: the six branches compared, how weapon upgrade offers work, the 50+ upgrade trees, evolution routes and branch unlock steps.
meta: Covers sephiria weapons / weapon upgrades / tier list / unlock dagger intent at branch level.
body:
Sephiria has six weapon branches, and each one carries a deep upgrade tree — the store listing advertises more than 50 unique upgrades per weapon. There is no seventh starter weapon: the scythe people search for is a Dagger conversion, explained on the scythe page.

The six branches at a glance

WeaponIdentityBest fitMain tradeoff
Sword and ShieldDefensive close meleeFirst runs and pattern learningShort reach
GreatswordHeavy, wide meleeCreating space and clearing groupsLong commitment per swing
DaggerFast reaction meleePrecise counters and bossesExtremely short reach
CrossbowRanged positioningKiting and safe damageReload discipline
KatanaAggressive meleeHigh ceilings once parry timing is learnedSteeper mastery curve
Staff / QuarterstaffVersatile casterFlexible damage at most rangesWants upgrade support to scale

How weapon upgrades actually work

  • Upgrades are offered, not bought. Each branch has a large pool — the advertised figure is more than 50 unique upgrades per weapon — and you pick from what the run shows you.
  • Offer rates differ by branch. Community 1.0 data reports Greatsword upgrades appearing more often than Dagger upgrades, which is why best also means actually completes.
  • Routes chain. An enhancement can convert one weapon skill into another: on Dagger, the frost line runs Dormant Frost into Drifa, and Drifa converts Blizzard Hammer into Blizzard Scythe.
  • Endpoints have names. Community routes end at named evolutions — Frozen Smelt from the Dagger frost line, Minigun from the crossbow lightning line, Creaking Spine from the greatsword line, Biryuu on Katana, and the elemental fusion staff on the caster line.
  • Presets remember the shape. Once a run works, a preset lets you rebuild it without re-deriving every pick.

Upgrade routes people finish

RouteBranchSteps as the community writes them
Blizzard ScytheDaggerDagger → Dormant Frost → Drifa, which converts Blizzard Hammer into Blizzard Scythe
Frozen SmeltDaggerDagger → Sleeping Frost → Frozen Smelt
MinigunCrossbowHeavy Crossbow → Unstable Lightning Mark → Minigun
Creaking SpineGreatswordSteel Greatsword → Bone Mechanism Sword → Creaking Spine
BiryuuKatanaKatana → Biryuu
Formless DanceStaffStaff → Throwing Spear → Formless Dance
Elemental Fusion StaffStaffStaff → Flame Staff → Elemental Fusion Staff
Route names and intermediate steps come from community reporting at 1.0.x. If a step is never offered in your client, the pool has changed — the branch is still the thing to commit to.

Unlocking a branch (Staff example)

  1. Progress to the chapter that opens weapon training.
  2. Buy the weapon training node on the Destiny Inscription tree with Sapphires.
  3. Talk to the village training-ground NPC, finish the short training ground, and the weapon appears on the village rack.
Exact sapphire costs and node names shift between patches — confirm in your client Journal or Destiny UI before committing a save's Sapphires.

Are the tier lists trustworthy?

Tier lists for Sephiria disagree because they are editorial and version-bound. One 1.0 list puts Greatsword and Staff at the top and Sword and Shield near the bottom; a later 1.0.30 meta list reorders the same branches and puts Katana and Greatsword first. Both are community rankings, not official TEAM HORAY tiers.

Use them to pick a branch to learn, then judge by whether your offers complete a route — see the builds page for which routes people finish.
